name: ID-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+13) with long-serving incumbent Mike Simpson seeking reelection
Simpson holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage over Democrat Ellie Gilbreath
No public general-election polling; prediction markets price the Democrat near 4%
Minor-party and Libertarian candidates on the ballot but with negligible funding
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Simpson: a Republican-leaning seat, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with markets pricing a Democratic win at only a few percent. With no polling to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate of a mid-teens Republican margin.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major outside-spending push into the district, would be the first sign this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern Idaho's second district is a Republican-leaning seat, and longtime incumbent Mike Simpson is running for another term after easily securing renomination. His campaign has raised over $1.1 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic challenger Ellie Gilbreath has raised about $107,000. No outside groups have reported spending in the race so far.

There is no public general-election polling to lean on, and no major expert ratings list the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give the Democrat only a small chance of winning. A Libertarian and two independents are also on the ballot but lack resources. All available evidence points to a comfortable Simpson reelection.
